punchline: The gang's own notebooks showed foot soldiers earning under $6 an hour while the leader averaged $63,000 a year.
thirty_sec: An ex-member handed two researchers the books of one Chicago gang set, four years of accounts. In one of their papers, street sellers earned under $2,000 a year on the books, under $6 an hour even with side sales, while the leader averaged $63,000. The authors concluded that hope of climbing the ranks helped keep the low-paid members in. It is one set's ledger, but it shows how a pyramid pays.
